title: Session handoff relay lineage is persisted and validated
acceptance: Handoff creation is a Main-owned sessions.createHandoff action that re-reads the authoritative Task Ledger handoff_from chain instead of trusting the renderer preview.
Cycles (self and multi-hop), conflicting parents and truncated ancestor walks are refused; unreadable Task Ledger history fails closed before any session is activated.
The lineage event (parent, root, depth, parentHandoffId, rootHandoffId) is persisted BEFORE the new conversation is activated, so a failed write cannot leave an untracked live session.
The depth limit is opt-in runtime.handoff.enabled with optional maxDepth (1-64, implicit 3) and defaults OFF; subagent maxSpawnDepth and frozen product values are unchanged.
New denial states are localized in en/zh/ja/ru; the runtime config type/schema/help/labels and the exhaustive parity fixture stay aligned.

autoreview.firstPass: 4 accepted findings (P1 post-persistence fork ordering hazard, P2 canonical session-key equality, P3 fresh-session key format, plus Main-accepts-unreadable-lineage concern) - all fixed
autoreview.secondPass: blocked: review engine returned HTTP 402 (budget pool quota exhausted) on 2 attempts; NOT a clean result
autoreview.note: The 402 is an external review-engine capacity limit. The runtime rules forbid switching engines and forbid landing on a prior review alone, so this is recorded as an open verification gap rather than claimed as clean.

boundaries: sessions.fork keeps its existing Gateway contract: this change deliberately does NOT add ledger lineage to forks, because writing lineage after the Gateway has already persisted the child leaves an untracked fork on failure. Fork-vs-handoff lineage reconciliation is separate work.
TF-0284 additionally requires context-pressure recovery and a broader independent full-chain acceptance; this issue closes only the handoff-lineage half and does not mark TF-0284 done.
No frozen default, product lock, release or publication change.
